title: Latex-ite Airport Grade Driveway Sealer Review: 2-3 Years
metaDescription: Latex-ite Airport Grade lasts about 2 to 3 years per two-coat job on sound asphalt, a solid mid-priced filler sealer at 250 to 350 sq ft per pail per coat.
h1: Latex-ite Airport Grade Driveway Sealer Review
keywords: is ultra shield a good asphalt sealer
intro:
Latex-ite Airport Grade driveway sealer is worth buying if your blacktop is structurally sound, has started to turn gray, and you will do a proper prep day first: owners commonly get about two to three years from a two-coat job. It is a polymer-modified filler sealer, so it goes on thicker than bargain pails, looks deep black, and its label claims resistance to gasoline and oil drips.

It is not a repair product, and it is not the right buy for every driveway. This review covers the verdict, who it suits, how far a pail goes, how long a coat really lasts, how it stacks up against Black Jack and Ultra Shield, and the handful of mistakes behind almost every bad Latex-ite review.
quickAnswer: Buy Latex-ite Airport Grade for a sound, weathered asphalt driveway that sees cars and the odd oil drip. Plan on roughly 250 to 350 square feet per 4.75-gallon pail per coat, two coats, and a reseal every two to three years. Skip it on brand-new asphalt, on driveways with alligator cracking, and on concrete. If you want the heaviest film for a rough, neglected surface, Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 builds more per coat at a higher pail cost.

sections.heading: Latex-ite Airport Grade Review: The Short Answer
sections.body:
| Question | Short answer |
| --- | --- |
| Is it good? | Yes, a dependable mid-priced filler sealer for sound asphalt |
| Who it suits | Weathered, graying blacktop with car traffic and oil drips |
| Coverage | Roughly 250 to 350 sq ft per 4.75-gal pail per coat (check your pail) |
| How long it lasts | About 2 to 3 years per two-coat job, per owner reports |
| Main rival | Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 for heavier film on rough surfaces |
| Skip it if | Asphalt is new, failing, or the driveway is concrete |

The verdict is simple: Airport Grade is a good product that gets blamed for bad prep. It carries enough mineral filler to close up hairline checking and worn texture, enough polymer to flex through a cold winter, and a fuel-resistance claim that helps on a garage apron.

What it will not do is hide wide cracks, hold onto a dusty or damp surface, or outlast a sealer applied in one heavy coat on a cool evening. Get the surface clean, dry and crack-filled, apply two thin coats in warm weather, and it does exactly what the label says.

sections.heading: What Is Latex-ite Airport Grade Driveway Sealer?
sections.body:
Latex-ite is the driveway brand of Dalton Enterprises, a Connecticut company that has sold asphalt maintenance products to homeowners and contractors for decades. The brand name points at its original idea: asphalt sealer with added polymer (latex rubber in the early days) so the dried coat bends with the pavement instead of cracking like a brittle film.

### A filler sealer, not a thin emulsion

Airport Grade is the formula most people mean when they say Latex-ite. It is a water-based asphalt emulsion loaded with fine mineral filler. As you pull it across the driveway with a squeegee, that filler drops into surface pores and hairline cracks. The result is a thicker film and a more uniform black than a budget sealcoat, at the cost of fewer square feet per pail. You are paying for solids, not water.

### What the Airport Grade name means

The name borrows from fuel-resistant coatings used on airport aprons, where spilled jet fuel would soften plain asphalt. On a home driveway the practical meaning is smaller: the label says the cured coat resists gasoline and motor oil better than an unmodified emulsion. That helps if you park an older car that weeps oil, refuel a mower on the driveway, or keep a motorcycle near the garage door.

### Fuel resistant is not fuel proof

A drip wiped up the same day will not soften the coat. A puddle left for a week will still stain and can lift the film. Keep a bag of absorbent in the garage and clean spills promptly.

### Is it coal tar?

Read the safety data sheet for the exact pail you buy. Formulas can vary by region, and several states and many towns restrict refined coal tar sealers. If the SDS lists an asphalt emulsion binder, you have the lower-toxicity type most homeowners should want.

sections.heading: Who Should Buy Latex-ite, and Who Should Skip It?
sections.body:
Latex-ite earns its price on the right driveway and wastes money on the wrong one. Walk your driveway in bright sun before you buy.

### Buy it if

- The asphalt is structurally sound: no web of connected cracks, no soft or sunken spots, no crumbling edges.
- The surface has faded to gray, individual stones are starting to show, and water darkens it rather than beading.
- A car, truck or small engine drips oil near the garage.
- You live with real winters and want a coat that flexes rather than crazes.
- You will set aside a prep day for cleaning, crack filling and drying.

### Skip it if

- **The driveway is new.** Fresh asphalt needs months to cure out its oils before any sealer goes on. Our guide on [when to seal a new asphalt driveway](/when-should-you-seal-a-new-asphalt-driveway/) gives the wait.
- **The pavement is failing.** Alligator cracking, potholes and broken edges are base problems. No sealer fixes them; you need patching, an overlay or replacement. Our page on [sealing asphalt pros and cons](/sealing-asphalt-driveway-pros-and-cons/) helps you decide if sealing is still worth it.
- **The driveway is concrete.** Asphalt emulsion does not bond to concrete and peels in sheets. Use a penetrating repellent instead, covered in our [concrete driveway sealer rankings](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/).
- **The surface is young and smooth.** A thin budget emulsion every couple of years costs less per square foot and does the job on tight, dark asphalt. Filler you do not need is money spent on nothing.

### What about heavy-duty use?

People ask whether Latex-ite works on a loading dock apron or a driveway that sees delivery trucks. It is a residential DIY product. Heavy trucks turning in place will wear any homeowner pail quickly. For commercial traffic, a contractor-applied sealcoat with sand and additives is the realistic choice.

sections.heading: How Much Does a Pail of Latex-ite Cover?
sections.body:
Filler sealers cover less ground than thin sealcoats because the solids stay on the surface. As a planning figure, expect roughly 250 to 350 square feet per 4.75-gallon pail per coat. Use the low end on rough, porous, older asphalt that drinks the first coat, and the high end on smooth surfaces sealed within the last few years. The pail label lists the range for that exact formula, and it is the number to trust.

### Pails for common driveway sizes

| Driveway | Area | Pails per coat | Pails for two coats |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One car, short | about 300 sq ft | 1 to 2 | 2 to 3 |
| Two car, typical | about 600 sq ft | 2 to 3 | 4 to 5 |
| Two car, long | about 1,000 sq ft | 3 to 4 | 6 to 8 |
| Turnaround or rural | 1,500 sq ft and up | 5 to 6 | 9 to 12 |

### How to do the math

1. Measure length times width for each paved area, including the apron and any parking pad, and add them up.
2. Divide by the label coverage for one coat, using the low number if the surface is gray and open.
3. Double it for two coats.
4. Add one spare pail and keep it sealed. Home centers generally take back unopened pails within their return window.

### Do not stretch it with water

Unless the label names a specific dilution, do not thin Airport Grade. Water lowers the solids you paid for and shortens the life of the coat. If your numbers come up short, buy another pail.

### What it costs overall

Pail prices shift with the season and the store, so check the current price where you shop. For the full picture, including squeegee, brush, mixing paddle, crack filler and a contractor comparison, see [how much it costs to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/).

sections.heading: How Long Does Latex-ite Last on a Driveway?
sections.body:
Owner reports most often put a well-applied, two-coat Airport Grade job at about two to three years before the driveway needs another coat. Some driveways in full sun with light traffic go a little longer. Shaded driveways, heavy vehicles and rushed prep get less.

### Where it wears first

Tire tracks, the turning area in front of the garage and the plow line go gray first. That is normal for any DIY sealer: a car turning its wheels while stopped grinds the top of the film. Spot-coating those areas after a season can stretch the full reseal interval.

### What shortens its life

- Sealer laid over dust or a driveway that was still damp from washing.
- A single thick coat instead of two thin ones.
- Application on a cool day or before a cold night, so the coat never cured properly.
- Rain within the first several hours.
- Driving on it before it set.

### Planning the cycle

Plan for a reseal every two to three years and check the driveway each spring. The water test is quick: sprinkle water on a dry day. If it beads and runs, the coat is still working. If the surface darkens and soaks it in, it is time. Our guide on [how often you should seal your driveway](/how-often-should-you-seal-your-driveway/) explains how to read the wear.

### Drying time

Foot traffic is usually fine after several hours in warm sun. Cars need at least a day, and two is safer, with more time in shade, humidity or cool weather. The full breakdown is in [how long driveway sealer takes to dry](/how-long-for-driveway-sealer-to-dry/).

sections.heading: Latex-ite vs Black Jack: Which Driveway Sealer Is Better?
sections.body:
Black Jack, made by Gardner-Gibson, is the brand Latex-ite most often sits next to in the aisle. The fair comparison is Airport Grade against Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000, the top of the Black Jack line.

| Factor | Latex-ite Airport Grade | Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type | Polymer-modified filler sealer | Heavily filled, polymer-modified emulsion |
| Film build | Medium to thick | Thick |
| Coverage per pail | Moderate | Lower, especially on rough asphalt |
| Spreading effort | Moderate | Heavier |
| Fuel resistance | Called out on the label | Not its main pitch |
| Pail cost | Mid-range | Premium |
| Best for | Weathered drives with oil drips | Rough, neglected, open-textured asphalt |

### Pick Latex-ite when

The driveway is in fair shape, you reseal on a two to three year rhythm, a vehicle drips oil, and you want a coat that spreads without wearing you out. For most suburban two-car driveways, this is the better value.

### Pick Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 when

The asphalt has gone years without a coat, the surface is rough and gray, and you want the heaviest film you can get from a pail so the next reseal is further away. Expect a slower, more physical spread and buy for lower coverage.

### And Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop?

Rust-Oleum's blacktop filler sealer is close to Airport Grade in purpose and is often priced a little lower. Despite the EpoxyShield name, it is an asphalt sealer, not an epoxy. On a fair-condition driveway, the pail that is in stock and cheaper on the day can decide it. Our [asphalt driveway sealer rankings](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) compare more brands side by side.

sections.heading: Latex-ite Ultra Shield vs Airport Grade: Is Ultra Shield Worth It?
sections.body:
Latex-ite has sold a premium formula under the Ultra Shield name alongside Airport Grade. It sits above Airport Grade in the line, with a heavier polymer load and a longer service claim on the pail. Product names and formulas shift between seasons and retailers, so read the label on the pail in front of you rather than relying on last year's version.

### When the premium pail makes sense

Ultra Shield is worth a look if you know you will stretch the reseal interval toward three years or more, the driveway is cold-climate asphalt that takes a beating every winter, and the extra cost per pail does not bother you. Fewer recoats over a decade can offset a higher pail price.

### When Airport Grade is the better buy

If you reseal every two years anyway, the standard pail is the better value: you are paying for life you will not use. Airport Grade is also the easier pick to find, since it is the formula most stores carry by default.

### Is Ultra Shield a good asphalt sealer?

On a sound, properly prepared driveway, yes. The same rules apply as for Airport Grade: clean, dry, crack-filled asphalt, two thin coats and a dry forecast. A premium pail laid over dust peels just as fast as a cheap one.

### What a service claim really means

Years printed on the front of a pail are the maker's figure for ideal application. Treat them as a ranking within one brand's line, not a promise for your driveway, which has its own shade, traffic and winter.

sections.heading: What Else Is in the Latex-ite Line?
sections.body:
The Latex-ite name covers repair products as well as sealers. The exact lineup changes between seasons and stores, so treat this as a map of the types, not a promise that every item is on every shelf.

| Product type | What it does | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Airport Grade filler sealer | Thick, fuel-resistant topcoat | Sound, weathered asphalt with car traffic |
| Premium sealer (Ultra Shield) | More polymer, longer service claim | You want fewer recoats |
| Pli-Stix rope crack filler | Melted into cracks with a torch | Cracks about 1/8 to 1/2 inch wide |
| Pourable crack filler | Squeezed or poured into cracks | Many narrow cracks, no torch |
| Trowel Patch | Fills wide cracks and shallow low spots | Spot damage and wide, stable cracks |

### Pli-Stix is the one to pair with the sealer

Pli-Stix is a rope filler you press into a crack and melt with a propane torch. It sets into a rubbery seal that handles freeze-thaw better than most pourable fillers. It takes longer per foot and needs care around the flame, but on a driveway with a dozen medium cracks it gives the most durable DIY result in the aisle. Our [driveway crack filler rankings](/best-driveway-crack-filler/) compare it with Crack-Stix and the pourable options.

### Mixing brands

Using a Latex-ite filler under another brand's sealer is fine once the filler has cured. Pouring two different sealers into one bucket to stretch a job is not: they can separate and dry to different shades. Buy enough of one product for the whole surface.

sections.heading: How Do You Apply Latex-ite for a Finish That Lasts?
sections.body:
Nearly every peeling or streaky Latex-ite job traces back to prep or weather, not the pail. Here is the order that works.

### Day one: prep

1. Trim grass back from the edges and sweep or blow off all grit.
2. Scrub oil spots with a degreaser and rinse. If a spot stays tacky, coat it with an oil-spot primer. Our guide to [removing oil stains from a driveway](/how-to-remove-oil-stains-from-driveway/) covers the cleaners that work.
3. Wash the surface with a [driveway cleaner](/best-driveway-cleaner/) or a pressure washer with a surface cleaner attachment.
4. Fill cracks wider than about 1/8 inch and let the filler cure for the time on its label.
5. Let the driveway dry for at least a full sunny day. Check shaded edges by hand.

### Day two: sealing

1. Start once the dew has burned off and the pavement is warm. The label typically asks for air and pavement at 50 degrees F or more and rising, with no rain for about 24 hours. Our page on [what temperature to seal a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/) has the detail.
2. Stir each pail with a drill-mounted paddle until no sludge is left on the bottom. Stir again whenever you refill.
3. Cut in along the garage, walks and edges with a brush.
4. Pour a ribbon across the driveway and pull it with a squeegee in overlapping passes. Work in sections of a few hundred square feet and keep a wet edge.
5. Let the first coat firm up, then apply the second at a right angle to the first.
6. Block the entrance and keep cars off for at least a day, longer if it is cool or humid.

### Watch the forecast

Check the hourly forecast the morning you start, not three days earlier. If rain catches a fresh coat, our guide to [rain after driveway sealing](/rain-after-driveway-sealing/) explains how to judge the damage. For the whole process in more depth, see [how to seal a driveway](/how-to-seal-a-driveway/), and for timing by region, the [best time to seal a driveway](/best-time-to-seal-driveway/).

sections.heading: What Do Owners Say in Latex-ite Driveway Sealer Reviews?
sections.body:
Owner feedback on Airport Grade falls into a steady pattern.

### The praise

- **Looks.** A rich, even black that makes a tired driveway look new for the first season comes up more than anything else.
- **Hairline cracks disappear.** Two coats commonly hide fine checking.
- **Water sheds.** Owners notice rain beading and running off where it used to soak in.

### The complaints

- **It is heavy work.** The product is thick, and owners with long driveways often say spreading it took more effort than they expected.
- **Tire-path wear.** Some reviewers see gray tracks and scuffs at turning spots within the first year, the same pattern any DIY sealer shows where wheels turn in place.
- **Peeling.** Peeling reports almost always describe sealer over dust, over a surface still damp from washing, in cool weather, or in one thick coat.
- **Tracking.** A few owners mention sealer carried into the garage on tires or shoes before it cured.

### Reading reviews fairly

Longevity reports range widely, and that is useful information. A sunny driveway with light traffic and careful prep commonly gets two to three years. If a reviewer expected five years from one coat on a busy driveway, no pail at this level would have met that.

If you are still comparing, our roundup of the [best driveway sealer](/best-driveway-sealer/) picks covers asphalt and concrete, and the store guides for [Home Depot](/driveway-sealer-home-depot/) and [Menards](/driveway-sealer-menards/) show what else sits next to Latex-ite on the shelf.

mistakes.title: Leaving the filler at the bottom of the pail
mistakes.body: Airport Grade's mineral filler settles into a dense layer during storage. If you skip the drill paddle, the first half of the pail goes on watery and the last half goes on like mud. You get streaks, thin spots and a coat that wears unevenly within months. Mix until the bottom is clear and stir again with every refill.

mistakes.title: Treating the sealer as a crack filler
mistakes.body: The filler in the pail hides hairline checking and nothing more. Anything wider than about 1/8 inch needs a rope or pourable filler first, fully cured. Sealer poured into an open crack shrinks, splits in the first freeze and lets water keep reaching the base.

mistakes.title: Sealing the morning after a pressure wash
mistakes.body: Washed asphalt holds water in its pores for hours, longer in shade. Sealer on a damp surface cannot grip and often peels in sheets by the next summer. Give the driveway a full sunny day to dry and feel the shaded edges before you open a pail.

mistakes.title: Laying it on in one thick coat
mistakes.body: A heavy single coat skins over on top and stays soft underneath, then tracks and cracks. Two thinner coats, the first firm before the second goes on, cure harder and last longer with the same amount of product.

mistakes.title: Using it on concrete or brand-new asphalt
mistakes.body: Latex-ite is an asphalt product. On concrete it never bonds and peels, leaving a black mess that is hard to remove. On fresh asphalt it traps curing oils and can leave the surface soft. Use a concrete sealer on concrete, and wait the recommended months on new blacktop.

faqs.q: Is Latex-ite a good driveway sealer?
faqs.a: Yes, for a sound asphalt driveway that has started to fade. Airport Grade is a polymer-modified filler sealer that goes on thick, looks deep black and lists resistance to gas and oil on the label. Owners commonly get two to three years from a two-coat job. Most bad reviews trace back to dusty, damp or cold application, not the product itself.

faqs.q: How long does Latex-ite Airport Grade last?
faqs.a: About two to three years for a well-applied, two-coat job, according to owner reports. Sunny driveways with light traffic sometimes go longer. Tire paths, turning areas and shaded sections wear first. A single thick coat, poor prep, cool weather or early traffic can cut that short, so plan a two to three year reseal cycle.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Latex-ite Ultra Shield and Airport Grade?
faqs.a: Ultra Shield is Latex-ite's premium formula, with a heavier polymer load and a longer service claim on the pail, at a higher price. Airport Grade is the standard filler sealer most stores carry. If you reseal every two years, Airport Grade is the better value. If you want to stretch the interval, Ultra Shield is worth considering.

faqs.q: How many pails of Latex-ite do I need?
faqs.a: Measure length times width, divide by the label coverage, then double it for two coats. Airport Grade typically lists around 250 to 350 square feet per 4.75-gallon pail per coat, so a 600 square foot driveway needs about four or five pails for two coats. Use the low end for rough asphalt and add one spare pail to return unopened.

faqs.q: Is Latex-ite better than Black Jack?
faqs.a: It depends on the driveway. Latex-ite Airport Grade is the better value for fair-condition asphalt and spreads more easily, with a fuel-resistance claim. Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 builds a heavier film for rough, neglected surfaces but costs more per pail and covers less ground. For a typical suburban driveway sealed on schedule, Latex-ite is the sensible pick.

faqs.q: Does Latex-ite work on concrete driveways?
faqs.a: No. Latex-ite sealers are asphalt emulsions made to bond with blacktop. On concrete they leave a black film that peels and looks out of place. A concrete driveway needs a penetrating silane or siloxane sealer or a concrete acrylic. Buy the sealer made for the surface you have, and use two products if your driveway mixes both.

faqs.q: How long before I can drive on Latex-ite?
faqs.a: Wait at least 24 hours, and 48 hours is safer. Foot traffic is usually fine after several hours in warm sun, but tires need a firmer coat. Cool nights, shade and humidity all add time. Turning the steering wheel while parked on a fresh coat scuffs it fastest, so block the driveway entrance until the surface is firm.

bottomLine: Latex-ite Airport Grade is a dependable mid-priced filler sealer that does its best work on sound, graying asphalt with oil drips and real winters. It looks good, builds a meaningful film and lasts about two to three years when the prep and weather are right. Its weak points are shared by every thick DIY pail: modest coverage, a heavy spread and no tolerance for shortcuts. Choose Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 if your surface is rough and neglected, Ultra Shield if you want a longer interval, and skip sealing altogether on failing or brand-new asphalt.
